review_candidates.description: Why Mozilla? Mozilla Corporation is the non-profit-backed technology company that has shaped the internet for the better over the last 25 years. Now, with more than 225 million people around the world using our products each month, we’re shaping the next 25 years of technology and helping to reclaim an internet built for people, not companies. Our work focuses on diverse areas including AI, social media, security and more. And we’re doing this while never losing our focus on our core mission – to make the internet better for people. The Mozilla Corporation is wholly owned by the non-profit 501(c) Mozilla Foundation. This means we aren’t beholden to any shareholders — only to our mission. Along with thousands of volunteer contributors and collaborators all over the world, Mozillians design, build and distribute open-source software that enables people to enjoy the internet on their terms. About This Team And Role We’re building a new B2B business for Firefox— bringing a privacy-first, data-safe browser and productivity bundle to European organizations. You will independently own the regional field plan, budget and senior Sales partnership for the DACH region and broader EU enterprise market. You will turn named-account priorities into a focused portfolio of high-value executive and technical experiences, with particular attention to German-language delivery, local enterprise buying dynamics and works council-sensitive programs and assets. You’ll work closely with Sales, Channel, Product Marketing, and Content teams to bring our go-to-market strategy to life on the ground, and you’ll help build the processes and playbooks this team relies on as it scales from a small pilot into a full regional function. Design and run a small portfolio of high-touch programs, including executive roundtables, private briefings, technical workshops, pilot-readiness sessions and a deliberately selected set of industry events. Define the intended account outcome for every program: the target stakeholders, the desired meeting or next step, the pre-event engagement plan, the seller handoff and the follow-up assets required. Own the DACH and EU market field budget, agency and vendor relationships, timelines, risk and execution quality; use shared Mozilla teams and the European agency for production, localization, PR, web and media operations. Develop and localize program narratives and assets into German in partnership with Product Marketing and Content, ensuring relevance for enterprise IT, security, privacy, procurement and business stakeholders. Collaborate with Product Marketing, Analyst Relations, Content/Creative, and Demand Gen colleagues to keep messaging consistent across the channel mix. Develop locally appropriate programs and buyer materials in partnership with Product, Security and Solutions teams, ensuring technical and security claims are reviewed and validated by the relevant experts. Bring the voice of the DACH and EU market back to the team, including buyer concerns, competitor signals, account feedback and regional ecosystem insight; convert learning into better messaging, field playbooks and return-on-event decisions. Track and report on program performance, using pipeline and engagement data to refine regional tactics.
